translation_notes: The stratum's read: `if not (s, RDF.type, domain) in g:` -> `if not m{ {s} a {domain} }:` (`not in`, hence `not m{ }`), with `@graph g` once at the top.

The other three reads of the region are translated too, so every island is credited: `set(g.subjects(RDF.type, X))` -> `set(m{ ?s a X })` (arity 1, bare terms); `for s, p, o in g.triples((None, prop, None))` -> `for s, o in m{ ?s {prop} ?o }` (p was unused: the tuple loses one slot, the only restructuring); `for _, _, domain in g.triples((prop, RDFS.domain, None))` -> `for domain in m{ {prop} rdfs:domain ?d }`. The .union() of two sets stays Python: m{ } has no UNION. `a` stands for rdf:type (Turtle keyword, not in the closed construction list).

Fixture: ex:knows typed both rdf:Property and owl:ObjectProperty (the set() must not duplicate it; ex:bob gives two genuine violations), two domains of which one is satisfied, no domain, a domain with no use, subClassOf not followed, and neighbours that must not match (an owl:DatatypeProperty with a violated domain; a domain on a non-property). Mutants killed: `not` dropped, rdf:Property -> free type.
optimization_notes: optimized.py: the three nested loops and the append become one list comprehension returned directly, `violations` goes, `g.triples((None, prop, None))` becomes `g.subjects(prop)` (one subject per triple, so the multiplicity is kept), `g.triples((prop, RDFS.domain, None))` becomes `g.objects(prop, RDFS.domain)`, and `not (s, RDF.type, domain) in g` becomes `(s, RDF.type, domain) not in g`. The property set is still built once, by `set(...).union(...)`.
optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph g`, `set(m{ ?p a rdf:Property }).union(m{ ?p a owl:ObjectProperty })`, and `if not m{ {s} a {domain} }` for the existence test.

Exception to the symmetry rule, which only an island allows: the two inner generators (subjects of prop, domains of prop) are joined into ONE multi-pattern island, `for s, domain in m{ ?s {prop} [] . {prop} rdfs:domain ?d }`; the `[]` object keeps one solution per triple, as the original (checked: multiplicity preserved). The Python side keeps its two `for` clauses.
Not compressed: the union of the two property sets stays Python (m{ } has no UNION) and so does the negation (no FILTER NOT EXISTS in m{ }).
